findings.title: Missing await on async reserve_stock in reserve_fast
findings.explanation: reserve_fast() calls async reserve_stock() without await. The coroutine object is always truthy, so `if not ok` never triggers and insufficient-stock 409 is never raised. The reservation also never actually executes.

evidence.why: reserve_stock is awaited in reserve() but not in reserve_fast(), returning a coroutine object.

findings.title: Blocking requests.get in async remote_stock endpoint
findings.explanation: remote_stock() is async but uses blocking requests.get() with no timeout. This blocks the event loop for all requests and can hang indefinitely. Use an async client with timeout or run sync I/O in a thread.

evidence.why: async endpoint uses synchronous requests.get, blocking the event loop.

findings.suggestion: Use httpx.AsyncClient with timeout, e.g. `await client.get(url, timeout=5)`.

findings.title: N+1 database queries in order_details loop
findings.explanation: order_details() loops orders and issues one db.items_for_order() query per order. Latency and DB load grow linearly with order count. Batch-fetch items for all order ids in one query.

evidence.why: items_for_order is queried inside per-order loop causing N+1 queries.

findings.suggestion: Add batch query like `db.items_for_orders(_conn, [o.id for o in orders])` and group in memory.
